Former acting US Attorney of the Southern District of New York Joon Kim will run point on the investigation.
Mortonson said clients are rotating into Nvidia rival AMD ( AMD ), whose stock is up 13% over the past five days.
The endgame for Nvidia could involve more than just Huang leaving as CEO, Mortonson said.
"It could be restrictions of some markets even, you know, tighter controls from the Department of Commerce," he said. "Singapore has always been this country of entry into China underneath the table, so to speak. … I think the export controls get cleaned up. And historically Nvidia had about 20% of their revenue coming from China. I think that's shut off, definitely in the near term and maybe the long term."

articles.title_orig: Big Walk used AI to fix a bug. Now the indie gaming world is having a reckoning.
articles.title_zh: Big Walk used AI to fix a bug. Now the indie gaming world is having a reckoning.
articles.content_orig:
The last few years have seen significant debate over the widespread use of AI-powered tools in game development and the responsible disclosure of that usage to players. That debate has exploded into a full-blown controversy in the indie game development space this week, as Big Walk developer House House has publicly and belatedly disclosed minimal AI use in its popular co-operative puzzle exploration game.
This particular controversy has been brewing behind the scenes for months, as judges and jury members for the prestigious Independent Games Festival Awards discussed the issue in private discussion groups. But the debate started to break into public view on Monday when 19 members of the 50-plus-member jury released a signed statement outlining a stance “declining to vote for any game that uses generative AI in any capacity.”
Noting “a significant increase in the number of submitted games developer with generative AI tools,” the group of jurors called out AI’s ecological, economic, psychological, and labor harms in rejecting tools whose use, they said, is still “not a foregone conclusion in our industry.”
The jurors also urged the IGF as a whole to “adopt a strong anti-AI policy for future years that disallows games containing any AI-generated work.”
Although the jurors’ statement didn’t name any specific games, by Tuesday morning, one critical darling in particular was increasingly being noted as a central part of the debate. In a statement provided to Aftermath (and added to the game’s FAQ page shortly thereafter), developer House House admitted publicly that “LLMs were used sparingly” near the end of Big Walk ‘s development “to help work through some difficult technical challenges and bugs.”
That limited AI use—which House House says represents “well under 0.1% of Big Walk ‘s code—stemmed in part from a thorny Unity engine bug that was slowing the game down with “infinite length” shadows during some game situations. After consulting with a Unity engineer who determined a fix “wasn’t possible,” House House said it consulted an LLM chatbot, which suggested a possible fix that the developers “had to modify… extensively” into the 10 lines of code that ended up in the final game ( At least one social media user says the bug was indeed fixable with significant human effort, though).
House House said it didn’t disclose this LLM usage for Big Walk ‘s Steam release earlier this year because Valve “does not request disclosure of code or chatbot usage.” Indeed, Valve’s AI disclosure form for developers specifically notes that it is concerned with AI-generated content, not “efficiency gains” from “modern game development environments [that] have AI powered tools built into them.”
The IGF Awards make no such distinction for AI usage, however, which led House House to mention its AI-assisted bug fix in submitting the game for awards consideration. A version of that disclosure is being made public now because “it has become a matter of public interest,” House House said.
“This is not an endorsement of, or argument for, the use of AI tools, however minimal,” House House wrote. “We have some concern that voluntary disclosures like this might contribute to the normalization of this technology, or its treatment as ‘inevitable.’ We support the work of those who are trying to limit the harm generative AI is doing to videogames and our world, and apologize that Big Walk ’s LLM usage may not meet their standards.”
Learning of House House’s AI disclosure was particularly painful for some IGF judges who had previously felt a special connection to Big Walk . In a blog post discussing his feelings , IGF jurist Austin Walker called the game “an achievement” that was “remarkable” and “beautiful,” featuring puzzles that “capture a range of play that is largely abandoned by the digital form.” Fellow jurist Damon Reece shared in a blog post that the game is “seriously special to me” and that it gave him “a profound and powerful emotional reaction to being in a space that felt like home.”
But when it comes to IGF awards consideration, Walker and Reece were among those who said that even minimal use of AI tools overrode that deep and abiding respect for the work itself.
“We have our hands on the lever here,” Reece wrote. “This is pain that has to happen [emphasis in original] to try and steer our culture away from this. We need to choose to speak loudly and clearly on this, to prioritize human creativity and labour, to tell the culture and the world that this is unacceptable to us. To do otherwise is rank cowardice.”
This isn’t the first time AI usage has noticeably affected game award judging. Last year, the Indie Game Awards (which are completely separate from the IGF Awards) rescinded awards for Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 after the developers admitted that some in-game textures were made using AI tools (these were later patched out).
“The Indie Game Awards have a hard stance on the use of gen AI throughout the nomination process and during the ceremony itself,” they said at the time.
Since House House’s public disclosure, the anti-AI contingent of IGF judges has found plenty of support from disappointed Big Walk fans and industry observers. In the last few days, the game’s Steam page has been bombed with over 400 negative reviews, though Steam’s anti-review-bomb tools seem to be limiting the impact on the game’s overall “Very Positive” reception there.
But others feel House House’s relatively minimal use of AI here is being blown out of proportion. They say it’s important to differentiate between games that use LLMs as a last-resort technical fix, for instance, and others that lean heavily on AI to generate the bulk of their art, music, or the core of the game engine itself.
IGF judge Liz Ryerson wrote on social media that she didn’t find House House’s AI use to be personally disqualifying for the awards and that “the fact that many acted like there aren’t any levels to this and it’s all the same is bothersome to me.”
“To feel like someone gets punished a lot more for transparency about a smaller level of fuckup vs. just not even attempting to be honest or transparent at all is what bothers me,” she wrote.
Steam Hype staff writer and prolific Steam curator Dominic Tarason also pushed back against the idea that “House House need to be memory-holed and their work never spoken of again” as a “penalty for touching the Forbidden Device.” He said he considers Big Walk “very mildly compromised art” that is still “absolutely, unquestionably art and very human.”
“They spent years on that work of art,” Tarason added . “They asked a chatbot for two minutes how to fix a bug. That’s a ‘That’s lame, don’t do that again’ failing. … Some of you are acting like they’ve been convicted of high crimes against humanity, to be sealed away in the darkest oubliette until not even bones remain.”
But some have argued that using AI to fix a bug rather than hiring an expert to figure it out did make the game’s development at least a bit less human than it could have been. “House House aren’t laying off developers to replace them with Claude, and I’m sure they would be firmly against the mere thought of doing this, but we can also clearly see how their actions are part of the same problem,” AI researcher Mike Cook wrote on his blog .
Still, game developer, author, and professor Brendan Keogh wrote that he thinks “an extreme zero tolerance of any [generative AI] is ultimately counterproductive now. [There’s] a lot of anger at devs that feel deeply conflicted enough about their glorified Google search to disclose it, and [that is] encouraging those using it to actually steal labor to hide that use.”
As time goes on and AI tools are increasingly used in the building of major game engines , it may become increasingly difficult for anti-AI absolutists to avoid every game that has been touched by even a hint of LLM-generated code (if that use is even disclosed in the first place). articles.title_orig: American Airlines brings fresh food back to NY-Chicago first class for first time since 2019
articles.title_zh: American Airlines brings fresh food back to NY-Chicago first class for first time since 2019
articles.content_orig:
American Airlines said Wednesday it's bringing small, fresh "bites" to first class on flights between its hubs in New York and Chicago, the carrier's latest effort to win over higher-spending customers .
The changes start this month. Customers will be able to pick between two options, which include prosciutto and melon or apple cinnamon chia pudding for breakfast and a Thai noodle salad or mezze plate for lunch and dinner, American said Wednesday.
American last offered fresh food for first class on these routes in 2019, a spokeswoman said. Currently, customers in first class on these flights get a smaller, packaged snack. Airlines largely have limited food options for shorter flights, even in first class.
American has fallen behind Delta Air Lines and United Airlines in profits and investments in premium options. The airline has been working to step up those premium offerings in recent years with new cabins, lounges and plans for seatback screens on its narrow-body fleets.

articles.title_orig: ‘In Flanders Fields’: How a patriotic poem became an anti-war anthem
articles.title_zh: ‘In Flanders Fields’: How a patriotic poem became an anti-war anthem
articles.content_orig:
I admire the fact that Canadians truly celebrate the poppy on Veterans Day, or, as they call it, Remembrance Day. Our day of remembrance is Memorial Day, so shifting the poppy there makes sense, but it’s a symbol of World War I, from a poem by a Canadian doctor at the front.
I read somewhere that the poppies came up in profusion because the ground had been so torn up, but having only read that once, I file it under “maybe.”
In Flanders fields the poppies blow Between the crosses, row on row, That mark our place; and in the sky The larks, still bravely singing, fly Scarce heard amid the guns below.
We are the Dead. Short days ago We lived, felt dawn, saw sunset glow, Loved and were loved, and now we lie In Flanders fields.
Take up our quarrel with the foe: To you from failing hands we throw The torch; be yours to hold it high. If ye break faith with us who die We shall not sleep, though poppies grow In Flanders fields.
John McCrae did not outlive the war , but my favorite memoirist, Vera Brittain, did, and wrote of her experiences as a nurse near the front in her classic Testament of Youth . She survived, but her brother, his best friend and her lover were all killed, and she memorialized her fellow veterans in the wake of the war with The Lament of the Demobilized .
‘Four years,’ some say consolingly. ‘Oh well, What’s that ? You’re young. And then it must have been A very fine experience for you !’
And they forget How others stayed behind and just got on – Got on the better since we were away. And we came home and found They had achieved, and men revered their names, But never mentioned ours;
And no-one talked heroics now, and we Must just go back and start again once more. ‘You threw four years into the melting-pot – Did you indeed !’ these others cry. ‘Oh well, The more fool you!’ And we’re beginning to agree with them.
Another Canadian, Dave Whamond, marks the day with a poppy, and somewhat echoes Elly Patterson’s wish that children there would not know war, though Canadians served, and died, in Afghanistan despite Trump’s insulting claims , and have worn the blue berets of the UN in troublespots throughout the world.
Danziger, a Vietnam vet , marks the day with a Mauldinesque bit of dogface realism, and I suppose people are betting on the deployment, which sure feels like betting on other people’s deaths.
Then, too, who knows anything? The Pentagon is keeping a lid on reports of deaths and injuries to US personnel and the only photos I’ve seen of the massive destruction of our bases in the region were taken by soldiers and their families, since the press has largely been kept away.
This may be the first war we’ve had from which photographers were barred since before Matthew Brady took pictures of Civil War battlefields.
Matt marks the day with an indirect remark about politicians who show up for the memorials but seem to forget to show up for the battles. Britain hasn’t had a veteran at 10 Downing Street since Sunny Jim Callaghan (1976-79), who served in the Royal Navy in WWII, though I don’t know that any of them took the coward’s way out and falsified their medical records to avoid service.
I’m not in agreement with Murphy, having had veterans in my family for several generations, including my grandfather, father, uncle, son and, currently, grandson-in-law, plus having close personal ties to the Air Force. He’s right that service involves sacrifice, and, to reference Mauldin again, a certain amount of grousing is part of the game. But even my good friends and classmates who endured PTSD, homelessness, addiction and difficult recoveries, haven’t seemed sorry to have served, only to have suffered.
I was at a reunion a dozen years ago, talking to a couple who had been high school sweethearts. She was remembering how long they’d owned their house down the street from my mother, and came up with a date, saying, “That was when you got home from Vietnam.” I said I hadn’t known he’d been there, and that “I missed that party,” to which he replied, “You didn’t miss a thing,” and we continued talking about the house.
On the other hand, I worked with two guys in 1972, a Green Beret and a mud Marine, who had great stories to tell, but that was in the years before Vietnam vets learned that nobody else understands, and started keeping their stories to themselves.
It all makes me very sorry to serve up this
This morning’s newsfeed was a real bring-down, as the Republicans exercised their fading majority in the House to protect Pete Hegseth from the impeachment that had seemed such a sure thing 24 hours earlier.
Joyce Vance has a terrific interview with fellow-prosecutor Dan Goldman (D-NY), who led the first Trump impeachment and is very well positioned to explain the legislative legerdemain used to squelch Hegseth’s impeachment and the overall prospects for reviving it.
As he says, even if it had gone forward, getting the necessary two-thirds vote for conviction was unlikely. Still, the process of laying it all out in front of the voters who launched last week’s blue wave would have been valuable.
Brown riffs on a quote from Dr. Strangelove, “Gentlemen, you can’t fight in here! This is the War Room!” the difference being that  Stanley Kubrick was writing a bitterly hilarious satire and Hegseth really was sincerely hiding behind Dear Leader, with whom he has cooperated to shift our nation from seeking Defense to waging War.
Trump couldn’t have stopped the House impeachment process with an executive order, but his influence over the party was enough to spark the delay, which effectively leaves the Secretary of Greasy Kid Stuff in place until January, when the tides shift in both houses.
However, if the uproar becomes an embarrassing inconvenience, Hegseth may discover what it means to no longer be a favored player in a bloodsport. Dear Leader doesn’t like to back down, but he also doesn’t like to look foolish, and while he is impervious to the feelings of the “suckers” and “losers” buried under white crosses in France and under the intended shadow of his arch, if Hegseth’s presence begins to make him look bad, No-Tab Pete may find himself on the outside looking in.
Keep the faith, and trust in karma.
Mike Peterson has posted his " Comic Strip of the Day " column every day since 2010. His opinions are his own, but we welcome comments either agreeing or in opposition.
Excellent song choice for our time, as well as Veteran’s Day. Regarding war poetry, there is a great anthology called Men Who March Away, strictly dealing with World War I, mostly from a British perspective (I think that title is from Thomas Hardy). Because contrary to many American beliefs about World Wars, it was not strictly an American war in which we rapidly triumphed almost immediately.
Today’s THE WIZARD OF ID has a direct reference to the Vietnam War Memorial, and I have a Remembrance Day theme in FurBabies.
Lalo Alcarez salutes Latino veterans in LA CUCARACHA.
Nancy, I was wondering about what you meant by the second panel. Is it a warning the democracy itself could become something we memorialize as well?
I was already choosing among Sassoon, Owen, Britain, McCrae and Robert Graves. Poppies vs Not Poppies was relatively easy to handle.
it means they fought fir our freedoms. I was originally going to use a little known quote from Franklin D. Roosevelt,  but decided that this version was more suitable for  Remembrance Day and Veteran’s Day.
I read this poem by A. E. Housman in my high school senior English class. If not on the same page as “In Flanders fields”, it was on the next one. It was 1967. It hit hard.
“Here dead lie we because we did not choose To live and shame the land from which we sprung. Life, to be sure, is nothing much to lose; But young men think it is, and we were young.”

articles.title_orig: Hundreds of Schools in Italy Are Evacuated as More Bomb Threats Rattle Europe
articles.title_zh: Hundreds of Schools in Italy Are Evacuated as More Bomb Threats Rattle Europe
articles.content_orig:
Some 6,300 schools across Italy and more than 700 in Scotland and Northern Ireland have received bomb threats, according to local authorities.
In Italy a number of buildings were evacuated as a precaution but Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni said checks so far had not indicated any evidence of "concrete danger".
"These reports appear rather linked to a strategy intended to cause alarm and concern," she said on Facebook.
Scotland's education secretary Mairi McAllan said there was no risk to the public and specialist cyber-crime officers were working to identify the source of the messages. In Northern Ireland education officials told schools to remain open unless otherwise advised by police.
It is unclear whether the incidents are connected.
"As a parent and as a constituency MSP I understand just how concerning this will be for parents, for pupils, for carers and for school staff," McAllan said.
Scottish police had earlier said that the warnings were "immediately assessed" as hoaxes. However some local authorities confirmed that some schools had been evacuated.
"Our advice is that there is no requirement to evacuate schools or keep children away from education based solely on the content of the emails," Police Scotland said.
Italian officials said a single email appeared to have been sent on Wednesday to the inboxes of 6,300 out of a total of 7,476 state schools, and private schools were unaffected.
The message, said to be from a certain "Mikhail Andropov, leader of Vilayat di Misoginistan", caused alarm in many schools.
The BBC has seen the email sent to Scottish schools which appeared to have similar wording, and also referenced the name Mikhail Andropov, although as leader of a "Red Owl" project.
Italy's Education Minister Giuseppe Valditara said the incidents involving Italian schools were probably a "cyber-attack, not a genuine risk", adding that there appeared to be a clear strategy behind the rash of threats in across Europe targeting flights, supermarkets and even hospitals.
Italian airports along with airlines elsewhere in Europe were hit by a series of bomb hoaxes last week that prompted a series of scares, evacuations and widespread disruption.
Although a number of threats were claimed by an extremist misogynistic group, it later denied any link to the false warnings.
On Wednesday one Milan headteacher, Anna Bertato, told Italian media she had checked the email address of the sender online: "It was already classified as spam by a student at a university in Taiwan."
Another Milan headteacher, Massimo Nunzio Barrella, told Adnkronos news agency that he had immediately realised the email was spam when it arrived in his inbox at 08:59 and he decided not to evacuate his school and reassured parents who phoned in.
"The text seemed almost comical," said Barrella, "it was like a message from Martians: 'We have come to annihilate you.' I even had a bit of a laugh."
Although many schools were initially evacuated on Wednesday, the alarm was quickly lifted, and pupils were allowed to return to class. Some parents decided to take their children home for the day, but the majority of schools in Milan did not send their pupils home.
Some 280 school head teachers had already received threats in recent days, according to Italian reports.
In a statement, the head of the central Umbria region Stefania Proietti said "checks conducted so far in Umbrian schools have proved negative, and law enforcement is working rapidly and carefully to verify each report".

articles.title_orig: Trump Officials Clashed Over Megaspeed, Firm at Heart of Nvidia Affair
articles.title_zh: Trump Officials Clashed Over Megaspeed, Firm at Heart of Nvidia Affair
articles.content_orig:
Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent challenged Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick over his department’s reluctance to label Nvidia customer Megaspeed a possible national security threat in a Situation Room confrontation last week that illustrates the tension inside the Trump administration over Chinese access to Nvidia’s advanced chips, two people familiar with the matter told CNN.
Trump officials have long harbored concerns that Megaspeed has circumvented US law and funneled advanced chips into China — a prospect that Treasury staffers argued should land it on Commerce’s so-called entity list of China-connected companies that could pose national security risks. But the issue gathered newfound attention and importance in recent days when Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang admitted to an affair with a Megaspeed employee suspected of being a Chinese spy.
Senior Trump officials, including Lutnick, also were briefed months ago about Huang’s relationship with Alice Huang, a Megaspeed executive who the intelligence community suspected of being a Chinese spy, people familiar with the matter said.
But despite those warnings, Commerce has so far refused to put Megaspeed on the entity list, the people said.
Confronted on it by Bessent last Thursday, Lutnick did not immediately commit to taking any specific action, they said.
Axios first reported the Situation Room confrontation.
Megaspeed is a Singapore-based company that was originally incorporated in 2015 as a Chinese video game developer called 7Road International. But in the three years since Alice Huang became director and the company changed its name, it has become one of the largest buyers of Nvidia chips in Asia , purchasing more than $4 billion worth of its semiconductors, by some analyst estimates.
Megaspeed has denied any wrongdoing and said it is a “compliant and legal company.” China’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs called the allegations that Alice Huang was a Chinese spy “groundless speculation and an attempt to smear and malign China.”
The entity list represents one of the US’s most significant tools for preventing American firms from selling their products to foreign companies and organizations. But adding Megaspeed to the list could also risk inflaming tensions with China amid Trump’s efforts to manage the US’ trade relationship with the fellow superpower. The Commerce Department hasn’t added any company to the list in more than a year.
Representatives for the Treasury and Commerce departments did not immediately respond to requests for comment.

articles.title_orig: Pixel users are getting a major Android Auto update – and it rivals Siri AI
articles.title_zh: Pixel users are getting a major Android Auto update – and it rivals Siri AI
articles.content_orig:
Gemini Intelligence is spreading beyond the Google Pixel 11 lineup to the Pixel 10, the upcoming Motorola Signature 27, and several of Samsung’s Galaxy foldables and flagship phones.
Though Google often offers its most upgraded features to other Android phone manufacturers, there are some features that are Pixel-exclusive or come to Pixel users first. This time, Gemini Intelligence is coming to Android Auto, but only for eligible Pixel users.
Also: I’m an Android Auto ride or die – but Apple CarPlay beats it on these 3 features
Google’s blog post states that Pixel users with Gemini Intelligence can expect it to gather information from their apps and surface it to their car’s infotainment screen. Google’s example is that if a friend texts you asking where you’re meeting for Pilates, Gemini Intelligence can find the correct confirmation email and offer to send it with one tap.
To access Gemini Intelligence in Android Auto, the Gemini app and subsequent setup are required; it’s available in select countries to users aged 18 and older, and feature availability will vary.
With more context about your messages, emails, and calendar events, a more capable assistant can complete cross-app tasks while driving, such as “remind me to buy mom a birthday card before her birthday” or “which route to my dentist appointment will be the fastest?” I often use Siri AI in CarPlay for tasks like these, and Gemini operates the same way. However, these tasks require user input first; what makes an AI assistant in in-car software great is when it suggests tasks before you ask for them.
Siri suggests to me when I should leave my house for an upcoming event in my calendar, such as a dinner reservation, flight, or doctor’s appointment, based on traffic conditions. It looks like Gemini Intelligence in Android Auto will offer the same assistance. I’ve reached out to Google to confirm, and will update this article if I get a response.
Also: 4 wireless Android Auto adapters we recommend (and they’re cheap)
I find Siri’s upgraded capabilities most useful when I have a busy day and heavy Atlanta traffic is thrown in the mix. Sometimes people need information about where to meet up, but I don’t remember the exact name of the location or which street it’s on. It’s difficult to search through my old messages or emails while staying alert to crazed drivers on the interstate, so a smarter AI assistant comes in handy.
Though Gemini Intelligence in Android Auto is reserved for Pixel users, the upgrade follows a series of improvements Google has rolled out to its in-car software. Non-Pixel Android phones and Android phones without Gemini Intelligence can use Personal Intelligence , which connects Gemini across your Google Maps, Photos, or Gmail data.
Personal Intelligence users can ask Gemini to navigate to a restaurant with a specific cuisine or vibe, or search their photos to find a car wash they photographed last week. Gemini Intelligence is more proactive and expansive, drawing on more sensitive data from your phone, such as messages, while Personal Intelligence relies solely on data from your Google services.

articles.title_orig: Toyota’s Scion is back, starting with an American-made, 25-mph kei truck
articles.title_zh: Toyota’s Scion is back, starting with an American-made, 25-mph kei truck
articles.content_orig:
Toyota is reviving the Scion badge as an experimental mobility incubator—starting with an Indiana-built, 25-mph kei truck engineered for American fleets.﻿
Toyota is reviving the Scion badge as an experimental mobility incubator—starting with an Indiana-built, 25-mph kei truck engineered for American fleets.﻿
Toyota is dusting off the Scion badge for a radically different mission. Rather than targeting youth-market hatchbacks, “Scion by Toyota” is being positioned as an experimental mobility incubator — and its first vehicle is an authentic Japanese-style kei truck built in Indiana.
Kei vehicles, which are built to satisfy Japan’s light vehicle regulations, are enjoying surging popularity around the world, including here in the US. More than 30,000 used kei trucks have been imported into the US since 2020, with roughly 7,500 units entering the country each year. Even President Trump is a fan , telling reporters last year that he authorized the Department of Transportation to approve their production.
Toyota looks to be the first to test the American market’s appetite for the tiny trucks. The choice to use the Scion brand, which was discontinued in 2016 , would seem to indicate that the automaker is hoping to appeal to younger car buyers. But more than that, Toyota says it sees Scion as a testing ground for utility, outdoor adventure, and customization that wouldn’t typically fit in any of its other models.
When it lands in the second half of 2027, Scion’s KEI-01 sports a 660cc three-cylinder gas engine paired with a continuously variable transmission. It won’t win any drag races, but it should delivery enough power for stop-and-go driving while using a minimum amount of fuel.
It’s true super power comes from its diminutive dimensions. At roughly 11 feet long and under 5 feet wide, the KEI-01 is about half the footprint of a full-size pickup. It can easily thread through cramped alleys, narrow barn aisles, garden gates, or busy campus pathways where standard trucks can’t fit.
The truck features an on-demand 4WD system with a push-button locking mode. If you’re cutting across muddy farm turf, gravel work paths, or wet slush, power splits to all four wheels to keep the truck from spinning out or getting stuck.
Inside, the vehicle looks pretty cheap, with lots of black plastic and a noticeable absence of any premium materials. That will hopefully help keep the price nice and low — though Toyota hasn’t disclosed any trim options yet. Japanese imports typically range from $6,000 to $12,000.
Because it is certified under federal Low-Speed Vehicle (LSV) rules — also used for golf carts and golf cart-adjacent vehicles — its top speed is strictly capped at 25 mph. The truck bed features three sides that fold completely flat, removing the need to lean over high-metal sides to drop in cargo. The KEI-01 can hold up to 600 pounds of soil, tools, or gear, and can easily tow small utility trailers or mowers.
Unlike an open utility cart or ATV, this tiny truck has a fully sealed cabin equipped with both heating and air conditioning. The extended roofline gives drivers extra headroom, reclining seats, and interior storage behind the seats to keep tools dry and secure. True to classic Japanese utility imports, the steering wheel is on the right side of the cab. Beyond the cool factor, curbside delivery and stepping directly onto sidewalks or worksite shoulders is quicker and safer.
To make the KEI-01 to conform to the rules and regs of auto manufacturing in the US, Toyota is investing $34 million into its Princeton, Indiana manufacturing plant to stand up local assembly and add roughly 50 jobs. Production kicks off in the second half of 2027, but everyday drivers won’t be able to buy one off the lot immediately.
Scion by Toyota is launching the mini-truck strictly as a fleet-focused pilot program targeting corporate campuses, farms, municipalities, and local delivery operators, distributed through a specialized group of existing Toyota dealerships. While Toyota notes it may consider opening up sales to consumer retail down the road if demand justifies it, the initial rollout is very much treated as an experiment to evaluate real-world US utility.
The KEI-01 was joined by two adventure-themed concepts that show Scion’s new focus extends far beyond budget hatchbacks. The SxS Concept packs a 300-plus-horsepower hybrid turbo setup for high-speed off-roading, while the modular BKE Concept explores compact personal mobility. Together, they signal that Scion’s second act is aimed squarely at niche utility and experimental recreation.

articles.title_orig: Apple is shuttering its 28-year-old online community forum
articles.title_zh: Apple is shuttering its 28-year-old online community forum
articles.content_orig:
Apple’s online community forum will close on November 20.
On Tuesday night, Apple posted a message to the Apple Support Community announcing the forum’s closure:
The Apple Support Community will permanently close on November 20, 2026. Starting today, the site will no longer accept new posts and is available in a read-only state.
You can continue to find trusted guidance and support on the official Apple Support site .
We want to thank the community members who have contributed their time and expertise to help others with their Apple products.
For 28 years, the forum has provided Apple users with a way to get quick technical advice about their products. That advice usually came from fellow users, though Apple employees occasionally chimed in. As with any community forum, the helpfulness and accuracy of the advice varied.
Apple reportedly told MacRumors that it is shutting down the forum after evaluating its support strategy and customer needs.
The Apple Support Community dates to 1998, when the online forum was known as Apple Tech Exchange. Two years later, Apple renamed the community forum to Apple Discussions. In 2011 , Apple revamped the forum, adding dedicated communities for specific devices and the ability to track responses to posted questions, while renaming it Apple Support Communities. By 2022, the forum was called Apple Support Community, as MacRumors noted this week.
Based on yesterday’s announcement, it seems Apple now prefers that its customers rely on official Apple employees for technical support. The forum may also have become less popular as rival forums grow, including Reddit and the technical support communities on the MacRumors and AppleInsider forums.

articles.title_orig: Gibran Rakabuming Raka: Indonesia's vice president resigns amid signs ruling alliance is fraying
articles.title_zh: Gibran Rakabuming Raka: Indonesia's vice president resigns amid signs ruling alliance is fraying
articles.content_orig:
Indonesia's Vice-President Gibran Rakabuming Raka has submitted his resignation, an aide has told the BBC, in a move which could further strain the political alliance that helped propel President Prabowo Subianto to power.
It comes after Indonesia's Supreme Court ruled that a high-school document used during Gibran's 2024 election campaign was invalid.
The ruling prompted more than 100 lawmakers to support a parliamentary initiative that could have paved the way for proceedings to impeach Gibran.
The aide, Budi Arie, said Gibran's resignation letter was submitted directly to Prabowo on Wednesday. It remains unclear if it has been accepted.
Gibran has long faced controversy over whether his high school qualifications met legal requirements to run for office.
Having studied in Singapore and Australia, he had used an Indonesian equivalence certificate to demonstrate his educational credentials.
Indonesian law requires vice-presidents to have completed senior secondary school or its equivalent, but the Supreme Court found no evidence to prove Gibran had graduated.
"No evidence was found to show Gibran had a foreign diploma or certificate that could serve as the basis for equivalency with a senior high school or equivalent qualification," it said.
It also considered a Constitutional Court ruling from earlier in October which came to the same conclusion.
Gibran previously argued that undertaking university education was sufficient proof that he had completed senior high school.
On Tuesday, he asked for the chance to challenge the ruling and be given the opportunity to prove the legitimacy of his education credentials, State Secretary Prasetyo Hadi said.
Gibran's ascension to Prabowo's ticket in the 2024 election was part of an alliance formed between his father, outgoing president Joko Widodo - known as Jokowi - and Prabowo, his erstwhile bitter rival.
Gibran was 36 at the time, and only became eligible for candidacy after a controversial ruling by the Constitutional Court, which exempted him from the minimum age requirement of 40.
His resignation comes as tensions between Jokowi and Prabowo appear to have flared.
Since taking the presidency, Prabowo has shown little interest in pushing ahead with Jokowi's legacy project: the construction of Nusantara, a new capital. Instead, he has focused much of the state's resources on his own flagship programme to provide free school meals across the country.
In a series of personnel reshuffles over the past year, Prabowo has also shifted many Jokowi loyalists into new roles, including long-serving finance minister Sri Mulyani Indrawati.
Last week, authorities arrested presidential chief of staff Listyo Sigit Prabowo - no relation - on suspicions of wiretapping the president.
Prabowo sacked Listyo a day later, in what many pointed to as a sign of a crumbling alliance: Listyo, who formerly served as the national police chief, is widely considered a long-time ally of Jokowi.
Within the government, allegiances seem to be shifting. On Monday, three members of Prabowo's cabinet collectively resigned from the party led by Kaesang Pangarep, Jokowi's youngest son, citing their desire to focus on their duties in Prabowo's administration.
All this is unfolding at a particularly turbulent period in Prabowo's presidency. The  free school meals programme is struggling for funding, parts of Indonesia have recently battled the country's worst wildfires in a decade, and the national stock market faces crisis amid allegations of widespread market manipulation.
On Tuesday, students across the country staged demonstrations to protest against the government's handling of a range of issues, including the environmental crisis and corruption.

articles.title_orig: China select board deals with complicated issues
articles.title_zh: China select board deals with complicated issues
articles.content_orig:
China select board members had several complicated issues on their Nov. 2 agenda, not all ripe for decision. They decided three:
— Board members unanimously approved a new, less comprehensive proposal from Raegan LaRochelle to assist with developing China’s revised Tax Increment Financing (TIF) plan (see the Oct. 22 issue of The Town Line, p. 3 ). LaRochelle will receive $3,200 for about three weeks spent educating the select board and the public and working with them and Town Manager Rebecca Hapgood to identify town projects eligible for TIF funding. Her fee will come from the TIF account. — After discussion of the town’s partly-outdated Telecommunications Ordinance, board members unanimously accepted Harmoni Towers’ bond in the amount of $68,637.75. The bond is intended to cover the cost of removal when the tower the company has approval to build on Parmenter Hill becomes obsolete (see the Oct. 29 issue of The Town Line, p. 2 ). The bond amount did not have the professional engineer’s endorsement that the ordinance requires. Codes Officer Nicholas French said confirming removal cost estimates is “not what professional engineers do.” — By yet another unanimous vote, board members changed China’s HRA (Health Reimbursement Account) from the current administrator to Consumer Health Solutions, saving $470 and, Hapgood hopes, getting as good or better service.
The HRA is related to the town employees’ health insurance plan, topic of a quarter-hour discussion and no decision. The Maine Municipal Employees Health Trust currently offers five plans; China is enrolled in the middle one, in terms of employee costs and benefits. The town would save money by switching to a less generous plan.
Hapgood said with the HRA covering employees’ costs, like deductibles and co-pays, last year was the first year the town didn’t “make employees whole.”
She invited select board members to send her questions to be answered at the Nov. 16 board meeting. With open enrollment starting Nov. 15, she expects a decision on Nov. 16.
Another issue involving money and potential complications is dispatching emergency services. Currently, China uses the Kennebec Sheriff’s Office (KSO), which in turn uses the state system. This system, Select Board Chairman Brent Chesley said he learned at a meeting the previous week, is outdated, and the state won’t spend money to update it.
Therefore, KSO intends to switch to the City of Augusta’s dispatching service, at a higher cost.
Chesley was indignant about several aspects of the planned new system. Each town’s charge is based on a 1987 formula, 75 percent on population and 25 percent on call volume, which he said is contrary to state statute.
The formula also hurts China and Chelsea, two Kennebec County towns that contract for KSO patrols, Chesley said. Every time a KSO deputy calls in to check a license plate, China gets billed for a call.
Chesley was more indignant because he had learned that towns with their own dispatching service don’t pay the county anything. He said he asked at the meeting if there is a county service China doesn’t use, can the town be exempted from paying for it?
A final insult, he said, was when county officials proposed starting the new service – and billing for it – on April 1, instead of waiting for the towns’ new fiscal years to begin July 1.
The dispatch bill will be separate from the annual county tax bill, he said.
Also needing decision soon is whether to renew the contract for disposal of bulky waste and construction debris or to seek a new company. The current contract with Waste Management ends Dec. 31. Hapgood said Transfer Station Manager Thomas Maraggio is seeking prices from several services.
Board members heard of, but did not discuss, one more potential expense increase, for Delta Ambulance. The towns of Fairfield and Benton have notified Delta that they intend to stop using its service in February 2027. Delta officials will have to find some way to continue to pay bills without those two towns.
As the meeting ended, Hapgood reminded those present that all town departments will be closed Wednesday, Nov. 11, for the Veterans’ Day holiday; and Thursday and Friday, Nov. 26 and 27, for the Thanksgiving holiday.
The Nov. 16 select board meeting is scheduled for 6 p.m. in the town office meeting room.

SpaceX is counting down to make history with the launch of its Starship Flight 15 mission on Friday, Nov. 13 , with liftoff scheduled for 5:45 p.m. EDT (2245 GMT) at Starbase, Texas. Starship Flight 15 will attempt to land both Starship Ship and Super Heavy Booster. It will be the first-ever full recovery of an orbital rocket and spacecraft, if successful.
Follow our Starship Flight 15 coverage here as SpaceX completes its final prelaunch work for the launch, which will also deliver 26 new Starlink V3 satellites into orbit.

Happy Wednesday, Space Fans. We are now T-2 days away from SpaceX's planned launch of its Starship Flight 15 test mission, so I wanted to take a moment to give you a run down on what to expect.
Today, you can read my full guide to SpaceX's Starship Flight 15 launch here , which goes over what time and where to watch the launch online. Liftoff is on track for Friday, Nov. 13, at 4:45 p.m. CST, which is 5:45 p.m. EST (2245 GMT). But it ALSO (and this is new) includes what time to tune in a day later for the planned Starship upper stage (Ship) landing and catch by the metal "Chopstick" arms of its landing pad at SpaceX's Starbase facility in South Teas.
If you're wondering how the rocket's assembly is going, our Spaceflight Editor Mike Wall has this update on the Starship Flight 15 Super Heavy booster going through final catch tests yesterday. Flight 15 will mark the first time SpaceX will attempt to land and catch both the Super Heavy booster (which it has done several times) and the Ship from orbit.
If successful, it will be the first full recovery of an entire orbital rocket from space.
Hello, Space Fans, and welcome to our coverage of SpaceX's Starship Flight 15 test flight , the first ever to attempt twin landings of the Starship Super Heavy booster and Ship upper stage.
SpaceX has officially set the launch date for Flight 15 for Friday, Nov. 13, at 5:45 p.m. EDT (2145 GMT) . That puts launch just about 3 days away and Space.com will provide live coverage of the potentially historic flight, the first full recovery of an orbital rocket.
Space.com Spaceflight Writer Josh Dinner will be reporting live from near SpaceX's Starbase , Texas site for the launch, with myself (Tariq Malik), Spaceflight and Tech Editor Mike Wall and other team members tracking the flight remotely for you here. SpaceX has already test-fired the engines on its Starship Flight 15 vehicles.
Today, SpaceX moved Super Heavy Booster 22 , the first stage for Flight 15, to the launch pad for vehicle stacking. Here are some photos of that move:
Super Heavy moved to the launch pad at Starbase. Booster 22 is the first Super Heavy V3 booster planned to return to the launch site for catch and was used for final catch testing upon arrival, including a suspended squeeze test at catch height https://t.co/iYTX1e6DEH November 10, 2026

articles.title_zh: Hadean mantle depletion and 3.95-Gyr subduction implied by North China rocks
articles.content_orig:
Thank you for visiting nature.com. You are using a browser version with limited support for CSS. To obtain
            the best experience, we recommend you use a more up to date browser (or turn off compatibility mode in
            Internet Explorer). In the meantime, to ensure continued support, we are displaying the site without styles
            and JavaScript.
The scarcity of terrestrial rocks older than 3.9 billion years (Gyr) has hindered our understanding of Earth’s early evolution, fuelling persistent debates on how and when the first continental crust formed and plate tectonics started. At present, the only unequivocally documented >3.9-Gyr-old rocks are from the Acasta Gneiss Complex, Canada 1 , 2 , 3 . Here we report a 3.95-Gyr-old trondhjemitic gneiss from eastern Hebei, North China Craton, in which primary magmatic zircon records elevated δ 18 O values (average +6.77 ± 0.23‰) and positive ε Hf ( t ) values (weighted mean +1.45 ± 0.27). This suggests a low-temperature altered basaltic source that originated from a mantle depleted in the Hadean. In contrast to the low-pressure origin inferred for the roughly 4.0-Gyr-old Idiwhaa unit in Acasta 2 , the 3.95-Gyr-old trondhjemitic gneiss reported here exhibits geochemical signatures attributed to a high-pressure origin 4 . Thermodynamic and trace element modelling demonstrate that its parental magma formed by means of low-degree (8–16%) melting of basaltic crust at >1.6 GPa and 740–820 °C, suggesting rapid burial of (near-)surface-altered oceanic crust to mantle depths along a cool thermal gradient. We propose that this rapid burial was most likely achieved through a transient subduction event.

articles.title_orig: Meta’s Head of Infrastructure, Engineering to Step Down in 2027
articles.title_zh: Meta’s Head of Infrastructure, Engineering to Step Down in 2027
articles.content_orig:
Meta's long-time infrastructure leader will leave the company in the new year, setting the stage for a  recently hired former Amazon Web Services executive to oversee its massive data center technical operations.
Santosh Janardhan, Meta's head of infrastructure and co-head of engineering, revealed his upcoming departure on Wednesday in an internal memo obtained by CNBC. Janardhan, who has worked at Meta since 2009, said "it's time to pass the baton" to former AWS senior vice president David Brown, who joined Meta in July from AWS.
The executive move underscores Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg's efforts to expand the company's data center operations under newer leaders at a time of increasing investor scrutiny on capital expenditure spending by the social media giant and its hyperscaler rivals.
Brown will now formally lead Meta's infrastructure efforts and serve as chief technical officer of the Meta Compute initiative, which is spearheaded by the company's president and vice chairman Dina Powell McCormick and technical leader Daniel Gross. Zuckerberg is relying on these new executives to continue developing cutting-edge data centers and related infrastructure needed to support its AI ambitions.
The company said during its recent third-quarter earnings report that it expects full-year capex to fall in the range of $135 billion to $145 billion. Meta also logged negative free cash flow of $2.12 billion, which S&P Global Ratings noted as part of its decision in late October to revise Meta's credit rating from AA- stable to AA- negative.
Janardhan said in the memo that he will help support Brown through the first quarter of 2027 as part of "the transition."
"As we make the next set of choices about our priorities, this is the right time for Dave to take the lead in shaping that work," Janardhan said in the memo. "Dave has spent his career building and operating dependable infrastructure for a wide range of demanding workloads. He has the instincts, depth and judgment this moment requires."
Bloomberg News first reported on the executive transition.

articles.title_orig: OpenAI’s quarterly revenue reportedly crosses $10B for the first time
articles.title_zh: OpenAI’s quarterly revenue reportedly crosses $10B for the first time
articles.content_orig:
OpenAI is bouncing back from the doldrums it experienced earlier this year. The company’s quarterly revenue crossed $10 billion for the first time, thanks to strong demand for its recent AI models, Bloomberg reported , citing anonymous sources.
If true, that would represent an almost 50% jump from the $6.7 billion in sales the company reportedly recorded in the second quarter. That would also mark a sizable increase in its revenue growth rate, which was previously said to be about 18% between the first and second quarters of the year.
OpenAI’s profitability picture also appears to have improved, with its adjusted operating margin narrowing from -150% in the second quarter to -109% in the third quarter, the report said.
OpenAI, one of the first to commercialize AI models, wasn’t exactly struggling to continue growing its top-line expansion — 18% growth on top of $5.7 billion in quarterly revenue is massive by any measure, especially compared to most software businesses.
But it was seeing those gains be trumped by its archrival Anthropic, which has taken the lead in capturing the enterprise market for AI models and recently reported Q3 revenue of $17 billion . OpenAI’s broader focus helped it attract a large user base and gain popularity early on, and it says it has over a billion users , but it’s reasonable to assume most of those are free users or subscribers to its cheapest plans.
Still, the company lagged Anthropic in catering to enterprises, a market where the Claude maker has pulled ahead, at least in terms of revenue growth.
OpenAI has recently benefited from a combination of tighter pricing, discounts, improving models, and a greater focus on building more enterprise-focused products and AI agents that can help people complete tasks.
OpenAI has now reached an annual revenue run rate of $50 billion, according to Bloomberg. Meanwhile, Anthropic, which is seeking a $1.4 trillion valuation in an IPO likely to happen soon , said yesterday that its annual revenue run rate had increased by $10 billion within a month to $81 billion as of the end of October.
(Note that OpenAI and Anthropic calculate their annualized revenue differently: Anthropic counts sales made by its cloud partners, while OpenAI only reports its share of some sales through its partners.)
None of those figures are small, of course, but the companies are also competing with models from Meta, Amazon, Microsoft, and Google, as well as a plethora of cheaper but still highly capable models from open source AI labs, especially those from China.

articles.title_orig: China seeks 'tangible progress' in ties with US as top diplomat Wang speaks to Rubio ahead of APEC summit
articles.title_zh: China seeks 'tangible progress' in ties with US as top diplomat Wang speaks to Rubio ahead of APEC summit
articles.content_orig:
Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi spoke by telephone Wednesday with US Secretary of State Marco Rubio, emphasizing Beijing's desire to achieve "tangible progress" in relations ahead of upcoming multilateral leader gatherings.
"China is ready to strengthen communication and cooperation with the US side, properly handle differences and sensitive issues," Wang told Rubio, according to China's Foreign Ministry spokeswoman Mao Ning.
Beijing and Washington support each other in the "successful hosting" of the APEC Summit and the G20 Leaders’ Summit, and "work for tangible progress in building a constructive China-US relationship of strategic stability," said Wang.
Wang affirmed that China's broader policy toward Washington remains "stable and consistent" as both powers prepare for senior diplomatic engagements.
Chins said the call was "positive and constructive."
"Stable momentum of China-US ties did not come easily and is the two major countries' rational choice based on respective and common interests," said Wang, according to a statement by the Foreign Ministry.
The call comes as Chinese President Xi Jinping prepares to host regional heads of state for the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Economic Leaders' Meeting from Nov. 18 - 19 in China. The summit will gather representatives from 21 member economies, including US President Donald Trump and Russian President Vladimir Putin, amid reports of a potential trilateral meeting involving Putin in Shenzhen.
Xi and Trump, during their two summits this year in Beijing and Washington, have agreed to build a "constructive relationship of strategic stability based on respect, fairness and reciprocity," according to China.
The US State Department had not released a readout of the call as of 10.50 am Washington time (1550GMT).

articles.title_orig: US postpones ‘million-dollar’ China ship tax until January
articles.title_zh: US postpones ‘million-dollar’ China ship tax until January
articles.content_orig:
The United States has extended the suspension of port fees targeting China-linked shipping for another two months, keeping the measures on hold through January 9, 2027, according to a notice published Tuesday in the Federal Register.
The decision gives Washington and Beijing additional time to negotiate over Chinese policies affecting the maritime, logistics and shipbuilding industries.
The Office of the United States Trade Representative said the extension took effect November 9 and runs through 11:59 p.m. Eastern Time on January 9. It follows a one-year suspension that began November 10, 2025, under a trade agreement announced by President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping.
The pause also continues to cover additional duties on Chinese ship-to-shore cranes and other cargo-handling equipment specified in the agency’s earlier action.
China also extended its suspension of reciprocal port fees on U.S.-linked vessels until January 10.
USTR said the circumstances supporting the original suspension remain in place and that further discussions with China are needed.
The U.S. fees could amount to millions of dollars for a single vessel’s visit. A 50,000-net ton ship, for example, would owe $2.5 million in charges.
The measures arose from the U.S. investigation under Section 301 of the Trade Act of 1974 into China’s targeting of the maritime, logistics and shipbuilding sectors for dominance. The suspended fee categories include charges affecting Chinese-owned or operated vessels, Chinese-built vessels and foreign-built vehicle carriers.
In comments to USTR, supporters of the pause argued that it would avoid higher shipping costs, prevent commercial disruptions and provide time for negotiations. Some sought permanent suspension of certain fees, warning that their return could disrupt trade and harm U.S. exports.
Opponents argued that the fees are needed to encourage investment in American shipbuilding and related industries, including container manufacturing. Some commenters also urged USTR to treat cargo-equipment tariffs separately from maritime service fees and end the suspension of those tariffs.
USTR said the United States will use the additional negotiating period to pursue its concerns with China while continuing efforts to expand domestic commercial shipbuilding capacity, develop the workforce and cooperate with allies.
Why it matters: The reciprocal pause averts additional shipping costs and potential disruptions affecting not only U.S. and Chinese carriers but also businesses worldwide that rely on Chinese-built vessels. It gives importers, exporters and shipowners temporary relief while trade negotiations continue.

articles.title_orig: Credit card debt hits record high as Americans struggle with cost-of-living
articles.title_zh: Credit card debt hits record high as Americans struggle with cost-of-living
articles.content_orig:
Americans are increasingly turning to credit cards as financial pressures mount, new reports show.
Collectively, credit card balances climbed by $22 billion in the third quarter to a record $1.29 trillion, according to the Federal Reserve Bank of New York's latest household debt report , released Tuesday. Balances are up 4.2% from a year earlier.
Total household debt, including mortgages , auto loans and student loans , also expanded by $334 billion for the July-to-September period to a record $19.1 trillion.
"Overall debt has been growing," the New York Fed researchers said on a press call Tuesday. "This does reflect financial hardship out there."
The average credit card balance per consumer now stands at $6,678, up 2.4% year over year, a separate quarterly credit industry insights report from TransUnion found. The number of people with credit cards rose 2% to 178 million from 174.8 million.
Consumers often turn to credit cards in part because they are more accessible than other types of loans — even though the average interest rate on a new credit card offer is about 24%, according to data from LendingTree . Credit card APRs vary depending on the type of card, the issuer and the borrower's creditworthiness.
"Credit cards continue to be one of the most expensive ways to borrow," said Charlie Wise, TransUnion's senior vice president of global research and consulting.
Over time, an increasing share of new credit cards has gone to borrowers with lower incomes and credit scores, and "those accounts are now showing higher levels of distress," the New York Fed researchers said in a corresponding blog post .
Credit card issuers loosened their lending standards during the Covid pandemic, and delinquency rates rose in the years that followed, the New York Fed researchers said on the press call.
"Macroeconomic headwinds — namely high inflation and rising borrowing costs — have squeezed consumers, with inflation outpacing wage growth for low-income brackets," according to the New York Fed.
Meanwhile, the cost of living continues to climb, with Americans paying more for essentials such as groceries and gas.
Stubborn inflation has now stretched on for years, putting many households in an affordability squeeze. Costs for goods and services rose more than expected again in October, the Bureau of Labor Statistics also reported Tuesday.
"Higher prices and higher rates have pushed more people into debt," said Ted Rossman, principal consumer finance analyst at Money Management International, a nonprofit credit counseling agency.
Balances have continued to swell in the wake of the pandemic, and even though the growth rate is now slowing, "from a household finance standpoint, a lot of damage has been done," Rossman said.
The reports come on the heels of the Democrats' strong midterm results, when many voters expressed their dissatisfaction with the U.S. economy , according to Kyle Moore, chief economist at the nonpartisan think tank The Century Foundation.
"The throughline connecting so many of Tuesday's outcomes was a recognition that the American economy is failing American families," Moore said, referring to Election Day.

This is CNBC's Morning Squawk newsletter. Subscribe here to receive future editions in your inbox.
Hello, this is Leonie Kidd with today's edition of Morning Squawk.
CoreWeave is providing the tailwind for futures today, helping lift neocloud stocks, while a rebound for Nvidia is also supporting the chip space.
But is it enough to dull the lingering doubts around the AI trade?
CoreWeave shares are surging in premarket trading, up over 16% overnight, after the neocloud group posted a 168% spike in third-quarter revenue.
The group also lifted its 2026 guidance , driving other neocloud stocks higher.
But bear in mind that shares are down 65% from their May highs, losing over 40% of their value in the last month alone.
Nvidia shares are extending gains in premarket trading, up just over 3%.
The move is also supporting gains for Broadcom , AMD , Intel and Nebius .
Here are the key developments:
CNBC's Seema Mody spoke to sources within Nvidia who said Huang walked into the group's Santa Clara, California, headquarters on Monday to hold his regular meeting with top-level executives.
To go inside that meeting, read the full piece here on CNBC.com.
Anthropic is offering 825 million shares at a price range of $70-78 per share.
Sources close to the deal told CNBC the AI titan is planning to price on November 18 and trade on November 19.
CNBC's Morning Squawk recaps the biggest stories investors should know before the stock market opens, every weekday morning.
Subscribe here to get access today .
The House of Representatives has effectively voted down an attempt to impeach Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth.
The House, by a 211-204 margin, approved a measure that will refer the impeachment resolution to a committee, leaving little time for it to be acted on before Democrats take over in January.
Tokenization: The next evolution of the stock market
The U.S. equity market has repeatedly changed its underlying mechanics while the asset itself — a share of stock — has remained largely the same.
Trading moved from floors and phone calls to electronic venues. Settlement cycles compressed. Commissions fell to zero. Fractional shares and online brokerages expanded retail participation.
The next major change may already be underway.

articles.title_orig: Windows 11 KB5132061 KB5131087 November 2026 Patch Tuesday direct download links here
articles.title_zh: Windows 11 KB5132061 KB5131087 November 2026 Patch Tuesday direct download links here
articles.content_orig:
Microsoft is investigating reports of Windows 11 KB5132061 installation errors, including 0x800f0993, 0x80070306, and 0x800f0989. In our tests, we observed that the November 2026 Patch Tuesday update reaches 99% before it fails, and you won’t make any progress even if you reattempt the installation.
On November 10, Microsoft rolled out Windows 11 KB5132061 as part of this month’s Patch Tuesday cycle, which means it’s a mandatory security update with close to 700 critical Windows-specific security fixes, plus other improvements like a customizable right-click menu.
KB5132061 bumps Windows 11 26H2 to Build 26300.9974 and 25H2 to Build 26200.9974, and it’s supposed to take a few minutes to finish installing. Usually, a Windows update requires a single reboot, but this one may require two or more reboots because of a pending Windows Secure Boot certificate update.
Two or more reboots aren’t exactly a problem, but there’s a bug that’s preventing the November 2026 update from installing. On my PC, the update installed within a few minutes. But some users aren’t even able to get it to finish installing, and retrying doesn’t help.
“I’m stuck in a loop of installing KB5132061, but it’s repeatedly throwing errors such as 0x800f0993, 0x80070306, and 0x800f0989,” one user told Windows Latest, and there are dozens of similar complaints.
One user told us that the November 2026 update failed on four of their PCs with either 0x800f0989 or 0x80070306. They tried downloading the update manually and resetting Windows Update components, but it still failed.
Another user ran into 0x80070306 on two virtual machines and shared the following error:
“Installation Failure: Windows failed to install the following update with error 0x80070306: 2026-11 Security Update (KB5132061) (26300.9974).”
I’ve also seen reports of Windows 11 KB5132061 failing with 0x800f0993 and 0x800f0922. One person said it failed seven times, including once when they tried the offline installer from the Microsoft Update Catalog, before it finally installed on another attempt.
Of course, not everyone is affected. Some users have reported that the update installed without any errors, while others say it eventually went through after they restarted their PC and tried again.
Microsoft’s support document still says the company is “not currently aware of any issues with this update.” However, that doesn’t mean Microsoft isn’t looking at the reports, as I’ve been told the company is fully aware of the complaints and is investigating the root cause, including the possibility that Sandbox is responsible.
Windows Latest understands that Windows 11 KB5132061 installation issues could be tied to Windows Sandbox, so if you turn it off, you should be able to install the cumulative update without any trouble.
For those unaware, Windows Sandbox is one of the lesser-known features of Windows, and it lets you run apps in an isolated environment (virtual machine), with the idea of easily testing untrusted programs or downloads. It’s a great addition, and some might have turned on the feature without even realizing it, and now it’s causing the November 2026 update to fail.
One user who looked at their Windows installation logs noticed an error referring to a file used by Sandbox. On their PC, the update failed while Sandbox was enabled, but installed after they turned it off and restarted.
However, I’ve also seen a report from someone who ran into the error without having the option enabled. But if you use Sandbox and the update keeps failing, it might be worth trying:
If you just can’t get Windows 11 KB5132061 to install, you can also try downloading the update from the Microsoft Update Catalog .
If nothing else works, Windows 11 has a Fix problems using Windows Update option under Settings > System > Recovery . It’ll reinstall your current version of Windows while keeping your apps, files, and settings.
For now, Microsoft is looking into the reports, and we’ll update this article when we learn more.

His articles and research works have been referred to by CNN, Business Insiders, Forbes, Fortune, CBS Interactive, Microsoft and many others over the years.

articles.title_orig: JetBlue unveils new first class seats to bring back profits
articles.title_zh: JetBlue unveils new first class seats to bring back profits
articles.content_orig:
JetBlue Airways unveiled its new domestic first-class seats Wednesday as more of the country's carriers bet on the premium travel boom to make them profitable again.
JetBlue announced it would offer a domestic first class — BlueFirst — in December 2024 and plans to start flying aircraft with the new seats and full on-board product next month. The carrier showed off the new cabin at its home hub at John F. Kennedy International Airport on Wednesday. Retrofits will continue during 2027, CEO Joanna Geraghty told CNBC late last month.
JetBlue will have 12 of the seats on its Airbus A320 fleet and 30 extra-legroom seats, down from 42 of those options previously. Because the airplanes don't have ovens, JetBlue said it is offering an array of cold food options like sesame noodles, pastrami sandwiches and tortellini salad, though they vary by route.
The rollout comes as the New York airline tries to stabilize after last posting a profit in 2019. Last month, JetBlue executives sought to calm investors after shares in the airline hit a record low following a report that bondholders had contracted restructuring advisors.
"We have no intention, no plans to file for bankruptcy. We are not engaged with any restructuring company," Geraghty told CNBC in an interview on Oct. 27.
Geraghty told CNBC's Phil LeBeau on Wednesday that JetBlue has "met with a few of the creditors over the last couple of weeks as part of ... normal investor engagement." She said the company made it clear to bondholders that JetBlue doesn't need to reorganize.
The airline's shares are up more than 40% this month, more than other passenger carriers, as of midday Wednesday, though they are still off about 11% so far this year.
JetBlue is betting that resilient travel demand, especially for for roomier seats will help fuel its turnaround plan, which aims to get the carrier to an operating profit next year and $1 in adjusted earnings per share in 2028.
Airline executives have said they expect fares to stay elevated next year as they grapple with higher costs, including but not limited to fuel, such as labor and airport fees. Geraghty said Wednesday that even if fuel prices moderate next year, "I don't think fares are going to fall as much as people expect."
Airlines large and small are racing to outfit their cabins with roomier, more expensive seating options to help cover ever-higher costs, from jet fuel to labor to airport operation fees.
For example, a ticket in the new recliner first-class seats between Kennedy Airport and Fort Lauderdale-Hollywood International Airport in Florida is going for $847 roundtrip in the first week of March while standard economy is $446.
On Tuesday, budget carrier Frontier Airlines unveiled its new first-class seats, which will take up the first two rows, and said it would outfit its Airbus fleet with premium seating that have extra legroom and in-seat power through row eight. The airline will take out a row of seating on its planes to make the pricier ones fit, chief marketing officer Bobby Schroeter told CNBC in an interview Monday.
JetBlue last month reported it ended the third quarter with $2.2 billion in liquidity and that its unencumbered asset base is now $7 billion, including $2.8 billion in aircraft and engines.
JetBlue had total debt of $8.4 billion as of Sept. 30, the carrier said in its earnings filing.
Geraghty told CNBC last month there is a "fundamental disconnect between the narrative in the bond market and what our financial results actually demonstrate."
When asked whether JetBlue's eye on keeping costs down includes furloughs, layoffs or buyouts, Geraghty last month said "absolutely not."

articles.title_orig: John Kerry: America Must Now Follow China’s Lead on Clean Energy
articles.title_zh: John Kerry: America Must Now Follow China’s Lead on Clean Energy
articles.content_orig:
Former US secretary of state says most nations are ‘stumbling along’ while Beijing has ‘hugely accelerated’
Cop31 live – latest updates
China is leading the world in moving away from fossil fuels , and the rest of the globe – including the US – must now follow, the former US secretary of state John Kerry has told the Guardian, as Cop watchers wonder exactly how China is going to approach this year’s climate summit.
As Cop31 opens – this year the climate conference is in Turkey – there is plenty of speculation about whether China will finally step into the leadership role that it has long avoided. In its latest “five-year plan” adopted in March 2026, China for the first time pledged to “actively participate in and lead global climate governance”. Cop31 could provide the first indications Beijing is ready to put that rhetoric into action, something it has historically been reluctant to do.
Green energy is a vital component of the export engine that has kept China’s sluggish post-pandemic economy on track. The success of its exports stands in contrast to its failure to significantly boost domestic general consumption, a structural weakness that has persistently vexed leaders.
In 2025, clean-tech exports surpassed $220bn, and they should grow again this year; the world’s largest emitter is now the world’s leading supplier of clean energy technology. China accounts for about 85% of solar and 80% of lithium-ion battery supply chain production capacity, and in 2025, nearly 75% of electric cars were manufactured there.
Smart moves now by China would position it as a linchpin in a future electrostate world order, persuade rivals to cooperate, and solidify its influence in the global south.
Meanwhile other countries, including the US under Donald Trump, have fallen badly behind. Kerry said they would lose out economically – as well as putting the climate in further danger – unless they, too, embraced low-carbon power and rapid electrification. “The only country that has hugely accelerated is China. The rest of the world is stumbling along while Mother Nature is sending us more powerful signals every week, every day,” he said.
“[China] realised suddenly they had way too much dependency on oil and gas from other places, and they decided they needed to be independent. Other countries, since the war in Iran, and since the strait of Hormuz has been interrupted, have made a similar decision, and they’re moving independently. There’s been a massive uptick in deployment of renewables. Thank you, Donald Trump.”
For autocratic states without free and fair elections , seeing the economic benefits reaped by China would be the spur to adopt low-carbon growth, he added.
“They’ll see where the market is going, and they will recognise where the cheaper alternatives are. Even they can read a spreadsheet, and understand where costs are exorbitant [in fossil fuels], and where you have a better deal,” Kerry said. “Right now, renewables together with storage, together with some transitional gas, is cheaper and more effective, than just going with fossil fuels.”
He added: “The marketplace has made its decision and globally is moving to electrons, and electrostate status. People are going to electricity and they’re going to try to do that as clean as humanly possible. That’s the choice that I see being implemented in many different places. It is unstoppable.”
China has already said it wants Cop31 to discuss the free flow of green technology against a backdrop of “intensifying” geopolitical conflicts – widely seen as a reference to US and EU tariffs on items such as Chinese electric vehicles and solar products.
Li Shuo from the Asia Society Policy Institute (ASPI) puts it this way : “In a world where climate action was once seen as a constraint on growth but is now increasingly a driver of it, China faces a singular question: will it step into a leadership role not out of obligation, but out of self-interest?”
The summit’s presidency has promised this Cop will be one of “implementation and acceleration” – and when it comes to the green transition, nowhere has implemented or accelerated quite like China. As a result, emissions have been in a “flat or falling” trend since March 2024, analysis for Carbon Brief shows .
Beijing sees the energy transition as “central to economic modernisation and energy security, with significant implications for international influence”, said Kevin Tu from the Oxford Institute for Energy Studies. The wars in Ukraine and the Middle East and their effect on oil and gas supplies have only hardened that stance.
The conflicts have also highlighted the geopolitical implications of a planetary shift to green energy. In the fossil fuel era, the designation of the US dollar as the global trading currency for oil gave Washington “what has been termed the exorbitant privilege of being the global lender of last resort”, said Isabel Hilton, the founder of the specialist environment outlet China Dialogue.
after newsletter promotion
“Without that, the US position in the world looks weaker, and if you add China’s dominance of the supply of clean technologies and the supply chains that produce them, US dominance looks more vulnerable still.”
Meanwhile, President Xi Jinping describes China as a “doer and go-getter working for the cause of global development” and state media frequently showcase Chinese renewable projects in countries ranging from Indonesia to Pakistan and Kenya. The value of the green energy deals in China’s belt and road initiative in the first half of 2026 has already surpassed the total for the whole of 2025, a recent analysis showed .
Those countries could be useful allies if China can get the subject of tariffs into the talks. “China is likely to find support from Brazil, India, South Africa and other developing countries concerned about the costs and market-access effects of climate-related trade measures,” said Tu.
China has generally held back from policy ambition or agenda-setting at forums such as Cop. Its attitude to the plans to set a global target for electrification has been ambivalent, even though it would easily hit it, according to ASPI’s Kate Logan. Partly, China has an aversion to prescriptive outside targets, but it is also trying to navigate the divergent interests of its global south partners.
Yixian Sun, a professor of sustainability governance at the University of Bath, said: “I still think there is a mismatch between Chinese policymakers’ views on the role that China can play in global climate governance and international expectations on the influence that China should exert.”
If the world wants China to play a leadership role, the environment needs to change, and more trust extended, he says. “They have to be ready to accept China’s leadership, and I don’t think this is the case, especially for global north countries”.
Analysts will watch China’s actions around climate finance commitments and support for a “just transition” – a framework designed to secure workers’ rights and livelihoods in the move away from fossil fuels.
They will also be looking for signals Beijing will bid for Cop33 in 2028; officials are said to be trying to decide if hosting would be beneficial.
For now, said Logan, “China would be happy with a Cop that doesn’t necessarily produce anything monumental, but comes out with a relatively cooperative outcome … so no major drama.”
